predecessors.name: Kievan Rus'
predecessors.text: the east (left) bank of the Dnieper, the Chernigov land with Poltava, as the rus dossier draws Mstislav's share

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the principality's last Cliopatria shape; sacked by Batu in the winter of 1239 (Mongol invasion page), inside Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape of 1241

ledger.x: 1024: Mstislav, son of Vladimir the Great, arrives from Tmutarakan and founds the principality of Chernigov.
1036: Mstislav dies and Chernigov passes to Kiev.
1054: Yaroslav's death gives Chernigov, with Tmutarakan, to Sviatoslav II.
1239: Chernigov falls to the Mongols and its inhabitants flee north; 'Prince Michael of Kiev ... later lost Chernigov'.
1240: Cliopatria's last Chernigov shape; from 1241 the land is inside the Mongol shape.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'
wars.outcome: The Mongols sack Chernigov in the winter of 1239; its inhabitants flee north and the land comes under Mongol supremacy, which 'lasted into the 14th century'.

certainty.note: Forest, steppe and river frontiers (the Dnieper from 1024, the Oka side of the Murom lands, the Polovtsian steppe on the south-east) never fixed by treaty or survey; the Council of Liubech (19 October 1097) assigns princes to…
